item.content:encoded:
A pedantic nitpick..

Once a driver has entered SCP-704, it begins its active phase.

Not "a driver operating a vehicle", so anyone with a valid license turns this on even while on foot.
Yeah, yeah, I know that everyone knows what it means, but still. This is the organization that has to specify that they mean tin foil hats and not aluminum foil. They probably have a staff of pedants in a dungeon somewhere specifically to find gaps like this.

Why didn't the observers in the solo test hit the bike's remote kill switch? I think it's less the road and there own inattention/poor reflexes that killed them.

Rather than ban solo tests, revise protocol to use auto-kill switches that disable the vehicle when it gets within a quarter mile of either end of the road.

I'd like to see the following continuing tests, both because they are fitting in-universe and I think the results could be entertaining to read.

-remote piloted vehicles
-autonomous drones
-vehicles with more than one driver (like a driver's ed car rigged with passenger side breaks)
-a power wheels jeep, or similar barely-a-vehicle toy ride
-a purpose-built, crash-safe car designed to keep the passenger inside and unhurt no matter what. Would probably just teleport them out of the car and into a tree anyway, but wouldn't The Foundation like to know for sure?

item.title: Operational parameters
item.content:encoded:
If this thing only activates when motor vehicles are present, and specifically does not activate for pedestrians…

what happens if we send out a big bunch of pedestrians, have them stand a few paces apart all the way down the road, and then send out a car?

Or what if we send out a very slow motor vehicle, slow enough that a human can keep pace with it the whole time?

What if we drill a hole in the gas tank so that the car runs out of fuel and can't enter any of the challenges? What if we build a car that operates on beamed power, and then cut the power?

Pretty obvious that bicycles wouldn't activate this… are horse-drawn carriages safe?

What if we secretly program the car with the route so that it drives itself, and the steering wheel is a placebo?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nah, that's just one more SCP that has to force you to use it in order for there to be any danger.

It's far more entertaining in my mind to imagine the road actively bucking and writhing like some sort of terrible serpent that wants to fling you off and crush you. That's a much more terrifying situation, you don't die or suffer because you suddenly went crazy for no reason but because the circumstances are huge and unfair and it doesn't really matter what you do or think.

There can still be nutjobs who try to drive this road because they see it as a challenge. That's fine. But let them own their dangerous behavior rather than have it thrust upon them.
